I will describe my impressions of the encounter with this.

It has the appearance of a butterfly—a moth, perhaps—set aflame. 

Nay, allow me to rearticulate. It would be more evocative to say that the flame itself has taken the form of such an insect.

It is surrounded by a crowd of red, fiery sparks.

This brings to mind memories from my youth. Oft did I collect twigs only to set them ablaze to watch as the fire consumed them.

The very same embers that disappeared into the night sky can be observed from this entity.

Watching the little bonfire, watching the twigs turn into bright red lanterns, then into black soot—I could not help but reach out to appreciate its warmth.

Many share this sentiment, no? We need not touch the fire to know that it blisters our skin and burns our bones. Yet we still yearn for its heat, to grow nearer to it.

Perhaps I had mused as such as its blaze danced and flickered so gently before us.

Such is all I have to say.

→ Right, mate, but fancy speech doesn’t explain why you decided to stroll right under its nose and burn yourself to a crisp, does it?

→ We have garnered a piece of useful intelligence from his death, however. The ‘embers’ Yi Sang brought back could spread to others under certain circumstances.

→ … And it spread right onto you and burned your skin. Most people I know would have a little more intense reaction to getting burned alive.

→ Well, yes. But the pain was relatively manageable.
我将会在下文中描述它给我留下的印象。

其外形正如同一只蝴蝶，抑或是一只被点燃的飞蛾。

不，请允许我换种说法。如果说是火焰本身就具有这种昆虫的形状，倒是更为恰当。

其被一簇簇艳红的火焰所包围着。

这勾起了我少时的回忆。我常常将杂乱的树枝收集起来，然后点燃它们，就那么看着它们被火焰吞噬成烬。

从这实体中可以观测到那消逝在了夜空中的火种。

看着树枝上微弱的火苗，逐渐变成旺盛的火焰，而后又变为深黑的焦炭，我不禁伸出双手去感受它的温暖。

我们不都是如此吗？无需触碰火焰，便可知其能够灼伤肌肤，燃焦骨头。即便如此，我们仍渴望接触它，感受它的温度。

当火焰于我们面前翩翩起舞，从容不迫地飘散时，我不禁如此去想。

以上，结束报告。

→ 你说得对，但这些华丽辞藻并不能解释你为什么决定在它眼皮下闲庭信步，并把自己烧成一团灰，是吧？

→ 不过，我们从他的死中得到了一个有用的情报。李箱先生带有的“火种”在某些情况下会转移到其他人身上。

→ ……那火种就转移到了你身上，而且灼烧了你。我所认识的大多数人都会对被活活烧死反应更加强烈，你怎么能这么淡定？

→ 没错。但疼痛感相对可控。

I had an opportunity to engage it in combat.

We have learned that, with my last approach, its embers may latch onto our bodies and spread to others under particular circumstances.

It was a shard of information gained only by chance, but it will still aid us as we carefully work out a strategy against this foe. (This does not indicate self-absolution of responsibility. I apologize for acting without much discussion among us.)

Allow its wings to touch us, and it will impart its embers upon our bodies.

From my brush with it, I came to realize that its strength grew the more ember it held.

Thus, it follows that breaking its wings would allow us to take the offensive in this battle.

I propose that we welcome the embers from its wings to our embrace.

These flames… they do not burn; they only bring us warmth. Perhaps accepting them may be of benefit to us.

However, the burns that my fellows have suffered afore… I must wonder what has caused it to inflict such pain upon them.

I know not enough information to comment further.

Such is all I have to say.
我曾有与其交战的机会。

我们了解到，在我最后一次接近它时，它的余烬可能会附着在我们身上，并在某种特殊情况下扩散到别人身上。

这项信息是在偶然中发现的，但在我们认真研究对付这个敌人的策略时，它仍会对我们有所帮助（这并不意味着我在推卸我的责任。我为我没有经过充分讨论就擅自行动的行为而道歉。）

如果让它的翅膀触碰到我们，它就会把余烬传递到我们的身上。

从我与它的接触中，我意识到它拥有的余烬越多，它的力量就会越强。

因此，折断它的翅膀可以让我们在与它的战斗中占据主导地位。

我建议我们敞开怀抱接受它翅膀上的余烬。

这些火焰……它们并不会燃烧，只会给我们带来温暖的感觉。也许接受了它们会对我们有所益处。

然而，我的友人们之前所遭受到的灼伤……使我不禁发问，是什么致使他们遭受如此痛苦。

我知道的信息还不够多。

以上，结束报告。

I may have ascertained the method in which it ‘sparks’ the embers.

In hindsight, the answer was quite patently obvious.

To awaken the dying embers, to revive its flames, one must fan it until it rises.

There is a moment in which it flutters its wings with such strength that it creates a gust of wind.

Every ember near it explodes in size and assaults us as the unrelenting gust summoned in that instance makes it appear like a giant ball of flame.

The giant ball of flame, in turn, spreads the embers upon us, growing into a greater flame.

The embers then ‘ignite’, burning my fellows near me.

The more embers it has, the greater its strength grows. Perchance it would be to our benefit that we embrace the warmth…

… but do mind that allowing its gust to overwhelm us could be devastating. 

Then, such is all I have to say.
我似乎已经得知了“点燃”其余烬的方法。

回头想想，答案显而易见。

让落在枝头上的火花燃起火焰的方法不正是对其扇风直到其燃起吗？

有那么一瞬间，它猛地扇动翅膀，掀起一阵狂风。

它身旁的每一团余烬都会爆炸开向我们袭来，因为那一刻召唤出的无情狂风使得它看起来如同一团巨大的火球。

巨大的火球反过来又将余烬散布到我们身上，促成更旺盛的火焰。

随后余烬便被“点燃”，灼烧我身边的友人们。

余烬越多，它的力量就越强。也许我们拥抱接受它对我们有所益处……

……但请注意，若是让它招来的狂风压倒我们，那招致的后果将会是毁灭性的。

以上，报告终止。

Oi! I’ve got a few things to say about this bastard before I get to the report.

Where the hell are these… good for nothing… cottonhead… gossypium shite comin’ from?

Well… not that I expect these Abnormalities to ever be helpful.

But the things they give us from time to time… they’re supposed to be ‘gifts’ no?

What kind of ‘gifts’ help our enemies keep their balance no matter what? They must be takin’ the piss out of us.

Sorry, had to vent a little here. You understand, yeah?

… Hm. Anyway.

It just looks like a tree with a massive bundle of cotton on it. Appearance wise, it doesn't look any different from the last time we ran into it. Waving, luring us to approach... Same shite, different day, eh?

And its center… is red. Like it’s sucking up blood instead of water.

On its sides it’s got… wriggling stems? Roots? Whichever it is, it’s bloody creepy. 

Pretty obvious ploy, innit? I'm sure those vines are there to poke holes in us like straws and suck the blood out of our veins.

Let’s tear’em to shreds before they can do anything like that.
喂！我写这个之前有话要说。

这些棉花头明明没什么用处，为什么还总喜欢跑出来？

不过嘛……反正我们也不需要异想体之类的帮助。

这些家伙偶尔给我们的东西。是叫“礼物”来着？

帮助我们的敌人，让敌人不知疲倦的东西，那能叫礼物吗？

我简直无话可说了，所以写在这里。你们能理解我的对吧？

……嗯，总之。

嗯……它看起来像长得巨大的棉花。如同往常在远处挥手，和上次引诱我们的时候一模一样。

中间是……不知道是不是代替水而吸进的血显得十分鲜红。

茎……？根……？是什么都无所谓，反正那些长得很恶心的藤蔓在摇摇晃晃。

一看就知道，那些吸管一样的藤蔓会噗呲一下插进我们身体里大口吮吸我们的血，不是吗？

先从哪里开始把那些藤蔓砍光吧。

If you knew that the vines can’t be cut, then why didn’t you— Haah, nevermind.

Don’t seem like we can stop these vines by cutting ‘em, Clockhead. Not sure if we can even cut them, in fact. 

Can’t help it. There’s no way to avoid getting punctured by these annoying things.

Damn it, this chilling sensation of getting my blood sucked right out of my veins… it ain’t pleasant.

Not to mention that this thing begins to turn red after it’s sucked enough blood out of us…

… When it does turn red, expect it to use a powerful attack against us at any moment. We better finish it off before it tries anything.

I suppose it’s easier said than done. Tsk, it’s not like we can pull these straws off us once they hit us.

The only way is to beat it into submission like fluffing the cotton inside a pillow. What other option have we got?
不是，所以说根本砍不断……哈，当我没说。

钟表头，不管怎么说，这些结实的藤蔓好像不管我们怎么砍都解决不掉。

战斗的时候……好像也没法避免被这些麻烦的东西扎中。

妈的，血被一点一点的吸走真的很不爽……

虽然是理所当然的，但那东西吸了我们的血之后就变红了。

在那种状态下，它会摆好准备进行强力攻击的姿势，所以最好在那之前了结它……

大概没说的那么容易，啧。被插上的吸管好像也拔不掉。

除了竭尽全力像打棉被一样把它打倒之外就没有别的办法了吗？

According to common sense, plants with deep roots and a good supply of water grow to be resilient.

I remember that somebody once told me that common sense often doesn’t apply to Abnormalities…

… yet here it is. An Abnormality that common sense does apply to. Blimey…

I'm starting to figure it out, though. It’ll wallop whoever has the most of these straws in ‘em. I’ve had the pleasure of a first-hand experience with it, so I’m quite certain of that.

Oh, and here’s something funny.

This little shite gives ‘gifts’ that somehow help our enemies never get staggered…

But beating the living daylights out of it seems to stagger it no fuss. What an absolute muppet.

We have to kill it when we have the chance. If we miss that chance… I’ve no idea when we'll get a second one.

The point is, don’t dally. I think it fancies me—I’ve no clue why. But it keeps jabbing me with its straw vines.
根扎得够深，水吸得够多的植物都不太容易死来着？

然后……异想体不能用常识来判断，这话似乎有谁对我说过吧。

为什么只有这时候就又符合常识了，可恶啊……

啊，如果说有发现什么事实的话……它是从身上插着最多吸管的家伙开始打的？因为我亲自被打过，所以这条绝对不会错的。

还有，哈。这还有个有点搞笑的。

这混蛋，送礼物的时候会喜欢强行让我们的敌人不会混乱……

但是如果把它打进混乱的时候还是会混乱的对吧？搞笑的棉花头啊。

那时候就要抓紧时机痛扁一顿……不然错过机会的话看起来就没办法处理那家伙了。

反正不要拖太久。因为虽然不知道为什么……我身上总是插着最多的吸管。

Y’know what used to really irk me back home?

Going without a meal, begging and pleading just so I can borrow some money… I never really minded that kinda thing. Only took a moment to put stuff like that behind me.

What really got to me though, was… that look of contempt. Like I’m beneath them.

I thought I’d gotten over that. Thought I’d grown out of it, learned to endure, ignore, and move on.

… Until today.

That thing doesn’t even look like a person. I wouldn’t even know how to describe that floaty thing if someone asked me to. But…

You know what I mean, right? It’s got that… oddly demeaning gaze. At least that’s what it feels like.

It really got to me for some reason.

Weird, squiggly artsy fartsy-lookin’… Tsk. I think it’s making some odd metallic noise, too.

Kinda looks like it's made of gold, doesn’t it? We should scrap it and sell its pieces so we can grab us tons of gourmet beef for a barbecue party.

→ I must inquire: is the thought of food consumption all that you are capable of processing?

→ Hey, I spent most of my life hungry, ‘kay? I guess rich kids with full bellies and cushy homes won’t understand.

→ Mmm~ I understand! Beef always tastes good, hungry or not. Even though I’ve never been hungry before I joined the company, hehe.

→ That’s not what I— ha ha.
嗯……你知道我的出生地最让我火大的是哪里吗？

挨饿、借钱……只是这些还不会让人动摇。过段时间就会忘记了。

被轻视。这是我最讨厌的事。

虽然现在……我比起那时候性格要更成熟，能适当地忍耐。

……但我今天又感受到了。

它看上去都不像人类，那漂浮在空中的东西，就算你问我是什么我也答不上来……

明白吗？就像是有人用一种居高临下的奇怪视线看着我。

那让人很恼火。

它看上去像是个缠了好几圈的装饰品……啧，还老是听到奇怪的金属声在回荡。

它看上去像是黄金的，要是卖掉一点说不定能买几块上好的牛肉拿来开派对呢。哈。

→ 你是只想着吃吗。

→ 那是因为以前吃的不好~生活富足安逸的孩子们大概不会理解吧。

→ 嗯~是吗？我是来到这里之后才吃不好的，但牛肉不是一直都很好吃吗？

→ 不是那个意思啦。哈哈。

Haah… Yeah, I can tell that this one isn’t gonna be easy.

I was right on the money about its ‘look of contempt’. The thing just glared at the one that attacked it most... before suddenly switching to a different kind of look?

'Worthless wretch, your worth is not enough to even lay a finger on me.'

… that’s what it would’ve said if it had a mouth, don'tcha think? That’s the impression I got, anyway.

Oh, and… sometimes, a huge pair of hands would just burst outta nowhere and snatch one of us away.

Meursault got snatched last time… and we didn’t know what to do. And the thing just squeezed him ‘till it left nothing but what looked like crushed tomato puree behind...

Eeuughh… just awful, right? Anyways… the only way to free us is to literally smack the hand until it breaks. Didn’t know it’d be that straightforward, but yeah…

And uh, if the hands ever get me… please, please make sure to prioritize breaking its grasp, ‘kay?

Sure, dying is never fun. But if I’m going to die anyway, I’d rather not get panini pressed to death.
哈啊……看起来这次会挺累人的……

我一开始感觉到的轻蔑并没有错。在我想着“那家伙一直在看着攻击它的人啊~”的时候……它好像突然眼神一变瞪过来了？

连触及我的价值都没有的无力之人。

……虽然它没这么说啦。如果有嘴它说不定会这么讲？因为它的眼神是那样的。

还有……它偶尔会伸出超大的手，抓住我们中的一个。

之前默尔索被抓走了来着……但是当时不知道该怎么办，所以他就那样变得跟被压扁的番茄似的。

很过分吧？唔……总之，我觉得直接把那个手打断就能解救罪人了。这应该不是个要动脑子的方法……

要是我被抓走了，万一的万一发生这种事，就请全力打断那只手哦……

不仅仅是因为我讨厌死，更是因为我不想像被那样子压成肉酱。

Okay, so I thought about this for a sec. Its grabby palm attack and its gaze full of contempt… they’ve gotta be related somehow.

First things first: the palms don’t just randomly grab any Sinner.

We've been missing its logic and pattern this whole time. There’s a specific window where it grabs us if we attack its hands.

At first, I thought it was just plucking us one by one, like plucking weeds from a garden… going for the most annoying one of us.

You see the logic, right? If you could squash anything getting in your way into tomato paste, wouldn’t you?

Actually, it totally makes sense. Wouldn’t everyone?

… I guess it’s my fault for expecting these things to follow any common sense.

Oh, but I think we can use its palms to our advantage. During the fight, we managed to free one of the captured Sinners who had its gaze on ‘em.

And that seemed to… really catch it off guard.

Must’ve been a shock, huh? Watching us, who are supposed to be nothing but lowly wretches, actually breaking its grasp and freeing our friend… know what I mean?

It seemed dazed for a good while, too. And that’s when we managed to really hurt it.

Mmm… still, we have to let it gaze at us with that weird look if we wanna pull off something like that again.

I guess it’s all about managing the risk & return, y’know…?

Boy, good luck, Dante! Hope your head doesn’t explode tryna work out this mess. … Oh my, is that why it’s always on fire?

You know I’m just joshin’ ya, right? Hehe.

→ Though your intentions may not have been hostile, I believe it is inappropriate to ridicule the Executive Manager as you have done here.

→ Well, this isn’t anything new. If you want to tackle every instance of you guys making fun of me, you'll be lecturing Heathcliff all week. And then some.

→ I give him a fair share of warnings every time I get the chance, Executive Manager.

→ What I’m saying is that I’m okay with it, so there’s no need to do something like that…

→ Huh? Clockhead's scribbled something here. Oh... so that's why our resident stick-up-the-arse sighed at me earlier, eh?
我觉得啊，那东西用轻蔑的视线看着谁，和它的手抓向谁应该是有关系的。

总之……被抓过去这件事应该不是随机的。

只是我们不知道而已，大概是在某个时机攻击手的人就会被抓走吧。

我觉得把惹自己烦的东西像除草一样拔掉是很正常的。

把自己不喜欢的东西做成番茄酱的心理，我觉得也很自然。

事实上，确实理所当然吧。谁都会这么做啊？

……好吧，不是所有人都觉得这很合理的。

啊，但是也有好事的。我们解救了一名被轻蔑的视线注视的罪人。

然后那家伙……好像很慌张？

大概是因为自己轻视的那些下等生物居然被同伴给解救了……之类的吧？

可能是恍惚了，一段时间内它的攻击都变得很脆弱。

嗯……但是为了制造这种机会，就必须得让罪人感受那种视线才行吧？

虽然能重来啦，但也不是完全没有风险……

但丁的脑袋绝对会爆炸的……啊，是已经爆炸过才烧起来的吧？

哈哈哈，开玩笑的啦。

→ 即使没有敌对想法，这样开经理的玩笑也是不应该的吧？

→ 诶……现在才说？这么说那每天都得向希斯克利夫指正这一点吧，奥提斯？

→ 有机会我就会提醒他。

→ 我没事的，不用那么做也可以……

→ 啊？怎么？这是钟表头写的吗。怪不得那个喜欢指手画脚的家伙只是看着我叹了口气就走了……原来是这么回事？

Spiral of Contempt
轻蔑螺旋
